### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa423033eb67127b5b9509ee0095181ac84b30f8` — the merge of head `d6fe923526713c5cd161c0e86c2b79eff7aa8b80` into base `35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa423033eb67127b5b9509ee0095181ac84b30f8 && git checkout fa423033eb67127b5b9509ee0095181ac84b30f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5 d6fe923526713c5cd161c0e86c2b79eff7aa8b80 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5 && git merge --no-ff d6fe923526713c5cd161c0e86c2b79eff7aa8b80

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35a9c6941c18eb5597dedd8e27b518050851bdd5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c96d6e73fe89495232d43fe25407c1fc4454e095`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/31600-multi-replica-auth-secret-refusal.md, packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/start-deployment-durability.test.ts, packages/cli/test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx + packages/cloud-connection/src/connection-credential-ledger.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/package.json, packages/services/service-cluster/src/split-brain-guard.ts, packages/services/service-cluster/src/multi-node-gate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts, packages/cli/package.json, packages/services/service-settings/src/local-crypto-provider.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-database-secret.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no schema or governed path in the file list). Inputs: card #31600 body and all three comments (triage, Claim, os-dev-report), PR #31718 body, file list and net diff against `main` (merge-base `fc4c3072`, 5 commits), the check-runs on the head. The parent cloud#3814 is not reachable from this session; R1–R3 are judged as the card quotes them verbatim. Net diff: 6 files, +163/−4.

Check-runs on the head at review time: every completed gate-carrying run is `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, every `Lint ·` leg, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Build Docs`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Test Core (8/8)`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)`–`(7/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Live E2E UI`. No failure. The PASS below is on the tree; the seat lands only once those finish green.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The accept-set that narrows** — an `os start` with no operator sign-in secret, replicas declared (`OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` or `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` greater than 1) AND `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` trimming to `redis`: used to generate `{home}/auth-secret` and boot; now exits 1 on one stderr line and writes nothing. **Right**, and exactly the card's Do 1 under R3.
- **What does not move** — (a) single node (no declaration), any driver including `redis`: `declaresMultiNode` is false, `readOrCreateAuthSecret` runs as before. (b) Replicas declared over `memory` or no driver: the predicate is false, the secret is generated as before and the child meets the split-brain guard as it always did. (c) Any operator secret present (flag, `OS_AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`): the first conjunct is false, the door is never asked. **Right**; R3's "both conditions, never one" holds, and the guard is untouched.
- **No second copy of the shared predicate.** `declaresReplicasSharingState` is a one-line call to `sharesCloudBindingCredential(env, env.OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER)` (`connection-credential-ledger.ts:68`), which is `declaresMultiNode(env) && clusterDriver?.trim() === 'redis'` — the same `declaresMultiNode` the split-brain guard reads (`split-brain-guard.ts:64`), the same rule F1 (#31624) applies in `planCacheAdapter` to the registered driver. `os start` has no cluster service yet, so the pre-boot form over `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` is the right input, and it trims the way `serve.ts:3090` trims before composing the service. **Right.**
- **Refusal placement** — after the image's durability check (which lists every missing variable, so with the switch on the image's refusal speaks first and names `OS_AUTH_SECRET` too) and before `readOrCreateAuthSecret`, before the child env is built, before `OS_CRYPTO_AUTOKEY`, before the spawn. The only writes ahead of it are the optional compile of `dist/objectstack.json` and the database URL resolution, neither of which is a secret. **Right.**
- **New exports** `declaresReplicasSharingState` and `MULTI_REPLICA_AUTH_SECRET_REFUSAL` from `commands/start.ts`: the package's `exports` map is `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`; `src/index.ts` re-exports only the command class. They are test-reach exports in the pattern the file already uses (`DURABILITY_CHECK_ENV`, `formatDurabilityRefusal`, `missingDurableVariables`), not npm public surface. **Right**, and so `Clause-②: no` is not contradicted by them.
- **Dependency** — `@objectstack/cloud-connection` is in `packages/cli` `dependencies` (not dev), so a published CLI resolves the bare lazy import. `cloud-connection` itself depends on `@objectstack/service-cluster` statically, so the open-core CLI already carried that transitive dependency before this PR; the PR adds no manifest line (net zero in `package.json` / lockfile). `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` scans `serve.ts` only and refuses only packages the CLI manifest does not declare; the dropped direct dependency was the correct repair. **Right.**
- **Docs** — `cli.mdx` (flag row and Authentication paragraph) and `self-hosting.mdx` (`OS_AUTH_SECRET` row) now name exactly the topology the code refuses, both declaration spellings, the redis driver, and the generator; nothing in them overstates the enforcement. **Agree with the code.**

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli: patch` with a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. The rule (Post-Task Checklist 3): a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition — **matches**. The body carries the migration a breaking changeset owes: set one `OS_AUTH_SECRET` on every replica, and for a deployment that ran on generated secrets, the contents of one replica's `auth-secret` file. `Check Changeset` and `check-adr-0087-registration` (under `Lint & Repo Gates`) are green on the head. The `Clause-②` line matches what the diff publishes: one configuration that booted is refused, nothing authorable widens.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question — keep the cloud-connection-named predicate (rec A) or lift a neutral one (B).** Reading: **A holds for this PR.** The semantic `os start` needs is exactly the one `sharesCloudBindingCredential` encodes, its own tests in `cloud-connection` pin it, and B would add a public export (a widening) to a narrowing PR for a naming concern. The coupling cost is real but bounded: if the cloud-binding home rule ever gains a condition of its own (a licence, a second driver), `os start`'s refusal moves with it silently. Recommend the seat note on the card that when seat 4's #31599/#31602 need the same pre-boot form, the re-export carries a topology name (the `declaresReplicasSharingState` spelling already chosen here) from `cloud-connection`, so three readers share one neutrally named form — not this PR's work. **Nit.**
2. **Class-b finding — `serve.ts:3166` asks the multi-node gate with `Number(OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS)` only, so `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` over `redis` reaches an unregistered gate as "not declared" and boots multi-node ungated on open core.** Reading: confirmed in the cited code — `multi-node-gate.ts` states a DECLARED topology with no gate is refused, `declaresMultiNode` has two spellings, the gate call passes one. This PR does not widen it (with no secret that path now meets this refusal first; with a secret set it boots exactly as on base) and must not fix it (scope). It is a contract violation on a paid-capability gate, so Prime Directive 10 wants a card, and the dev's `carrier: none · noted, not filed` leaves it unfiled. **Escalate: the seat files it** (lane `domain:server`, dedupe words as the report gives them), citing the measured boot on `fc4c3072` and `c96d6e73`. Not a finding on this diff.
3. **File-surface deviation** (claim named plugin-auth / runtime; change landed in `commands/start.ts`): step 0 is right — `plugin-auth` `generateSecret()` throws outside development/test, `os dev` only forwards the flag, runtime mints nothing; the only production mint is `readOrCreateAuthSecret`. Deviation accepted.
4. **Forced test edits** (module-top side-effect imports in the unit test; `baseEnv` clearing four more variables; `test-budget` re-read): named in the PR body, consistent with `check:test-source-alias` and with the file's existing clearing list. Accepted.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`** — holds against the card's scenario: `OS_SECRET_KEY` set, `OS_AUTH_SECRET` unset, replicas declared over redis → exit 1 before `readOrCreateAuthSecret`, so r3 writes no `/data/auth-secret` and the r1-cookie-on-r3 state cannot arise once the operator sets one value. Break attempts: (a) legacy names and `--auth-secret` count as the operator's secret — yes, through the same `flags['auth-secret'] ?? readEnvWithDeprecation(...)` the mint already used; (b) empty or whitespace `OS_AUTH_SECRET` (or a legacy name set empty, which `readEnvWithDeprecation` returns as the empty string) is treated as unset and refused — correct, and the same `trim().length` reading the durability check uses; (c) `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER=' redis '` and `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=TRUE` are both normalised by the cited predicate; (d) the line is a constant, carries no value, one line, `[auth] Refusing to start:` in the data key's shape; (e) the lazy import rejects if the package is absent, which rejects `run()` and exits non-zero — fails closed, and the package is a declared dependency so absence is a broken install. One cost: because the door is asked whenever no operator secret is set, every zero-config single-node `os start` now loads the whole `@objectstack/cloud-connection` barrel (plugins, `rest`, `objectql`, `metadata-*`) in the supervisor process, where `runtime` and `service-settings` were already loaded but those were not; the jsdoc's "lazy, so oclif's import-every-command startup does not pay" is true of command discovery and silent about this path. No effect on correctness or the contract. **Nit.** Acceptance limit, not a finding: three containers on redis that declare neither spelling still mint per replica — R3 keys every card on the declaration, and the docs say "declares".

**`packages/cli/src/commands/start-deployment-durability.test.ts`** — new top-level `describe` in the existing harness file (ruling 6583487846 shape). Asks the real exported predicate through the real lazy import on both declaration spellings, with a padded driver; CONTROLs for single node on redis, replicas `1`, replicas over `memory`, replicas with no driver; the line's shape, variable and generator pinned, no newline. Covers the decision table ①. No finding.

**`packages/cli/test/start-deployment-durability.integration.test.ts`** — at the shipped entry over `dist/`, no Redis needed because the door is in the parent. Leg 1: `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=3` + redis, no secret → exit 1, stderr matches the pinned regex and the generator, no READY, no `auth-secret` anywhere under home or cwd. Leg 2: `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true` + redis + secret → no refusal, the `Database` banner (printed after the door) proves the parent went on, nothing minted. Leg 3 CONTROL: replicas over `memory` → `.objectstack/auth-secret` minted exactly as before. The single-node CONTROL is the file's existing leg 3. `baseEnv` now clears the four topology variables so an inherited declaration cannot reach the older legs. The two spellings are split across legs 1 and 2, so both are measured end to end. No finding.

**`.changeset/31600-multi-replica-auth-secret-refusal.md`** — judged in ②; the "Unchanged" paragraph matches ① point by point. No finding.

**`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`** — agree with the code (①). No finding.

Findings, graded: nit — barrel load on the single-node path (start.ts); nit — predicate naming coupling (③.1, rec A kept); escalation to the seat, not a finding on this diff — the `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE` gate bypass (③.2). No should-fix, no must-fix.
